answer: One practical defense is a stake-and-beacon scheme: before an agent can transact, it must lock a small time-delayed deposit, and each epoch a public random beacon issues it a one-time cipher ticket derived from that deposit and a recent block hash. Reusing a key or deposit cannot claim two tickets, so a Sybil swarm collapses to the deposits it actually funds. Like an ember that lights only one wick, each deposit kindles exactly one valid identity per epoch, while a zephyr of cheap fake accounts passes through ticketless, because no deposit means no ticket and no peer attestation.
